title: Fire and burning
examples: What are the three things needed for something to burn?
How can I stop a fire from burning?
What do we get when things burn?

explain.say: A fire needs three things to happen or continue burning.

draw.text: The Fire Triangle: Fuel, Oxygen, Heat

explain.say: The first thing is fuel, which is any material that can burn.
The second thing is oxygen, which we get from the air around us.
The third thing is heat, which gives the energy to start the burning.
When things burn, they create different products, like ash or smoke.
To stop a fire, you must remove one of these three things.

faq.q: What are the three things needed for a fire to happen?
faq.a: A fire needs fuel, oxygen, and heat. If you remove any one of these three, the fire will go out.
asks: Can you name the three parts of fire?
What do we need for combustion?

faq.q: What are the products of burning things?
faq.a: Combustion products can include ash, smoke, and sometimes heat energy. These are the things left behind or released.
asks: What do you get when wood burns?
Are smoke and ash the same thing?
What is left over after a fire?

faq.q: How can I put out a small fire safely?
faq.a: You can put out a fire by removing the fuel, cutting off the oxygen supply, or cooling it down by removing the heat.
asks: How do we extinguish a fire?
What is the safest way to put out a fire?

faq.q: Does the type of fuel change the products?
faq.a: Yes, different fuels create different combustion products. Burning plastic makes different things than burning wood.
asks: Does burning gasoline make the same ash as burning wood?
Are the products always the same?

faq.q: Is oxygen always the limiting factor?
faq.a: No, while oxygen is needed, sometimes the fuel runs out first, or the heat source is removed before the oxygen is used up.
asks: If I cover a fire, what am I doing?
Can a fire burn without air?
What is the most important thing to remove?

facts: Combustion is a chemical reaction that requires heat, fuel, and oxygen.
Ash is the solid, non-combustible residue left after something burns.
Smothering a fire removes the oxygen needed for combustion.
Cooling a fire removes the heat energy required for it to continue burning.

quiz.say: A campfire needs wood, air, and a spark to burn. Which element is the fuel?
quiz.why: Wood is the material that is actually being consumed and burned.

wrong.0: The spark is the heat source, which starts the reaction, but it is not the fuel.
wrong.1: Heat is the energy that causes the reaction, not the substance that burns.
wrong.3: Air is the source of oxygen, which is a necessary element, but not the fuel itself.

quiz.say: If you cover a small fire with a blanket, what element of the fire triangle are you removing?
quiz.why: Covering the fire cuts off the supply of fresh oxygen from the air.

wrong.0: The blanket does not remove the burning material, only the air around it.
wrong.1: Ash is a product of burning, not one of the elements needed to keep it going.
wrong.3: While the blanket might cool it slightly, its main job is to block the air.

quiz.say: When natural gas burns, what is a common product you might see or smell?
quiz.why: Combustion of fuels like gas produces carbon dioxide, which is a gas.

wrong.0: Water vapour is also a product, but carbon dioxide is the primary gas from hydrocarbon burning.
wrong.1: Oxygen is what is needed to burn, not what is produced by the burning process.
wrong.2: While carbon can be produced, carbon dioxide is the more common and expected product from complete combustion.
